answer: In PoA, each identity must lock collateral in a bonded escrow, and cryptographic evidence of coordinated equivocation links the offenders. For a detected group of k identities, the correlated penalty scales as O(k²), so splitting one operator across a sybil swarm does not divide its exposure. Asymmetric depreciation compounds the loss across linked escrows, applying an exponential multiplier on detection; onyx, nectar, and ivory denote distinct collateral classes, not exemptions from this rule.
